blogs.title: The Underdose Trap: Why 0.3 mg Epinephrine May Be Failing Our Adult Patients
blogs.description: This post dissects the critical tension between guideline-recommended epinephrine dosing (0.5 mg for adults >50 kg) and the ubiquitous reality of 0.3 mg auto-injectors in clinical practice. Using the case of a patient requiring multiple escalations due to suboptimal initial dosing, we analyze the evidence suggesting that underdosing increases the need for rescue interventions and delays stabilization, arguing for a paradigm shift in how we prescribe and administer epinephrine in the ED.

blogs.title: Beyond Biphasic: Navigating the Diagnostic Black Hole of Multiphasic Anaphylaxis
blogs.description: While biphasic anaphylaxis is a recognized entity, multiphasic recurrence (three or more episodes) remains poorly defined with no clear management algorithms. We explore the clinical challenges illustrated by this case, discussing how to differentiate true multiphasic anaphylaxis from refractory shock or ongoing antigen absorption, and debate whether aggressive preemptive IV epinephrine infusions are warranted versus an expectant 'wait-and-see' approach when symptoms wane.

blogs.title: The Steroid Question Revisited: Do Corticosteroids Prevent Relapse or Just Prolong Admission?
blogs.description: Traditional teaching holds that corticosteroids prevent biphasic reactions, yet modern evidence suggests they offer no benefit and may increase adverse outcomes. This post reviews the shifting landscape of steroid use in anaphylaxis, contrasting historical protocols with current meta-analyses, and examines why clinicians continue to prescribe them despite guidelines advising against routine use—particularly in complex, multiphasic cases like the one presented.

blogs.title: Mast Cell Disorders Unmasked: When Recurrent Anaphylaxis Signals Systemic Mastocytosis
blogs.description: Recurrent anaphylaxis without a clear trigger should raise suspicion for underlying mast cell pathology. This article uses the case's finding of elevated baseline tryptase and hepatomegaly to discuss the diagnostic criteria for systemic mastocytosis (SM). We highlight the pitfalls of missed tryptase sampling windows in acute settings and outline a practical workup strategy for identifying SM in patients with 'idiopathic' or recurrent severe allergic reactions.

blogs.title: Observation Protocols vs. Resource Reality: Defining Risk Stratification for Complex Anaphylaxis
blogs.description: With biphasic/anaphylactic recurrence rates varying wildly (0.4% to 23%), determining safe discharge timing is a major pain point in emergency medicine. We critique current observation window recommendations (4–24 hours) against the backdrop of limited healthcare resources. The post proposes a risk-stratified framework based on severity markers (e.g., need for multiple epi doses, hypotension) rather than arbitrary timeframes to optimize patient safety and bed utilization.
